skill_title: Apply the critical angle and total internal reflection

items.question: What is the critical angle?
items.expectedAnswer: The angle of incidence for which the angle of refraction is 90°.
items.explanation: At the critical angle the refracted ray travels along the surface (refraction angle = 90°).
options: The angle of incidence for which the angle of refraction is 90°.
The angle at which light passes straight through.

items.question: What is total internal reflection?
items.expectedAnswer: All the light reflects back inside the denser medium instead of refracting out.
items.explanation: Beyond the critical angle, light is completely reflected back into the denser medium.
options: All the light reflects back inside the denser medium instead of refracting out.
Light passes straight through the boundary.

items.question: What is the FIRST condition for total internal reflection?
items.expectedAnswer: Light travels from a denser to a less dense medium.
items.explanation: TIR requires light moving from a denser (higher n) to a less dense (lower n) medium.
options: Light travels from a less dense to a denser medium.
Light hits the surface along the normal.
Light travels from a denser to a less dense medium.

items.question: What is the SECOND condition for total internal reflection?
items.expectedAnswer: The angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.
items.explanation: The angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle for TIR to occur.
options: The angle of incidence is greater than the critical angle.
The angle of incidence is less than the critical angle.
The angle of incidence is exactly zero.

items.question: Which equation gives the critical angle?
items.explanation: The critical angle satisfies sinθc = n₂/n₁, with n₂ the less dense medium.

items.question: Optical fibres carry light signals using which effect?
items.explanation: Optical fibres rely on total internal reflection to keep light bouncing along the fibre.

items.question: At an angle of incidence exactly equal to the critical angle, the refracted ray...
items.explanation: At θc the refraction angle is 90°, so the ray skims along the surface.

items.question: Can total internal reflection occur when light goes from air into glass?
items.expectedAnswer: No — it must go from the denser medium to the less dense medium.
items.explanation: TIR needs light moving denser → less dense (glass → air), not air → glass.
options: No — it must go from the denser medium to the less dense medium.

items.question: Below the critical angle (smaller angle of incidence), what happens to the light at the boundary?
items.expectedAnswer: Most of it refracts out of the medium.
items.explanation: Below θc the light refracts out (with some partial reflection); TIR only happens above θc.
options: Most of it refracts out of the medium.

items.question: Total internal reflection only happens at the boundary with a...
items.explanation: TIR occurs going into a less dense medium, where the critical angle exists.

items.question: A glass has refractive index 1.5 and is in air (n = 1). Find the critical angle. (sin⁻¹(0.667) = 41.8°)
Water has refractive index 1.33 (air = 1). Find the critical angle. (sin⁻¹(0.752) = 48.8°)
A light ray inside glass (θc = 42°) hits the glass-air surface at 50°. What happens?
items.explanation: Since 50° exceeds the critical angle of 42°, the ray is totally internally reflected.
options: It refracts out into the air.

items.question: A light ray inside glass (θc = 42°) hits the glass-air surface at 30°. What happens?
items.expectedAnswer: It refracts out into the air (30° < 42°).
items.explanation: Below the critical angle (30° < 42°), the ray refracts out of the glass.
options: It refracts out into the air (30° < 42°).

items.question: A denser medium has a SMALLER critical angle than a less dense one. Why is this useful in optical fibres?
items.expectedAnswer: A small critical angle means more rays undergo total internal reflection, trapping the light.
items.explanation: A smaller θc means a wider range of angles cause TIR, keeping the signal inside the fibre.
options: A small critical angle lets light escape easily.
It has no effect on the fibre.
A small critical angle means more rays undergo total internal reflection, trapping the light.

items.question: Diamond has a very high refractive index (2.42) and so a small critical angle (~24°). How does this affect its sparkle?
items.expectedAnswer: Light is internally reflected many times before leaving, increasing the sparkle.
items.explanation: A small critical angle causes lots of total internal reflection, so light bounces around and exits brightly.
options: Light is internally reflected many times before leaving, increasing the sparkle.
Light passes straight through without reflecting.

items.question: A medium has critical angle 30° with air. What is its refractive index? (sin30° = 0.5)
Why does total internal reflection NOT occur when light goes from air into water?
items.expectedAnswer: There is no critical angle going from a less dense to a denser medium.
items.explanation: TIR requires denser → less dense; going less dense → denser, the ray always refracts in, so no TIR.
options: The critical angle is too large.
There is no critical angle going from a less dense to a denser medium.

items.question: An optical fibre's core must have a refractive index that is... compared with its cladding.
items.explanation: The core must be denser (higher n) so light travelling in it can totally internally reflect at the cladding.

items.question: At an angle of incidence just below the critical angle, the refracted ray is...
items.expectedAnswer: very close to 90° (nearly along the surface).
items.explanation: As the incidence angle approaches θc from below, the refraction angle approaches 90°.
options: very close to 90° (nearly along the surface).
